title: When not to invent a collection
hook: The BCL already has the pipe, the set, and the list. A custom “AsyncQueue” in a worker is usually Channel<T> with extra bugs. Name it, then wait for module 15.

sections.heading: Use the type that already exists
sections.prose: Need a growable buffer? List<T>. Need lookup? Dictionary<TKey, TValue> or FrozenDictionary after startup. Need uniqueness? HashSet<T>. Need FIFO in one thread? Queue<T>. Need a snapshot for many readers? ImmutableArray or ImmutableDictionary. Need a bounded in-memory producer/consumer between async methods? Channel<T> in System.Threading.Channels. Channel<T> is the standard library answer for “I have SQS-poll tasks producing Message and a processor consuming them inside the process.” Concurrency, WaitToReadAsync, and bounded capacity are module 15 (concurrency and threading). This topic exists so you do not spend an interview writing a lock around Queue<T> from first principles when the interviewer wanted Channel.CreateBounded<Message>(10).

snippets.label: Name Channel, do not implement it
snippets.explanation: If the data never leaves the process and producers are async, Channel<T> is the type. If you just accumulated one ReceiveMessage page, List is enough.

sections.heading: Do not wrap Redis or SQS in a fake IList
sections.prose: A Dictionary is not Redis. A Queue is not SQS. Implementing IEnumerable on a type that silently talks to the network on MoveNext hides latency and retries. Prefer an explicit client method that returns IReadOnlyList<T> or IAsyncEnumerable<T> (module 13) so the caller sees the I/O. Custom collections are justified when you have a domain-specific invariant (a ring buffer you measured, a specialized graph). They are not justified because you wanted a class named MessageBag.

sections.heading: Interview cue
sections.prose: If asked “how would you coordinate producers in one process?”, say Channel<T>, then ConcurrentQueue if they constrain you to older APIs, then lock+Queue as the last sketch. If asked “how would you store tenant feature flags for the lifetime of a Lambda?”, say Dictionary or FrozenDictionary loaded at startup, backed by Redis if it must be shared across instances. Inventing a new collection type is a smell unless you can name the invariant List cannot express.

interviewTakeaways: Prefer BCL generic collections; ArrayList and Hashtable are legacy.
Channel<T> is the in-process async queue — details in module 15.
Do not disguise I/O as IEnumerable unless the contract is explicitly a stream (module 13).
commonPitfalls: Writing a thread-safe list with public lock fields.
Exposing ConcurrentQueue as a substitute for SQS and losing durability.
Building a custom enumerator that hits Redis on every MoveNext.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Node streams / async iterators are the analogue of IAsyncEnumerable and Channel, not of Array.push in a loop.
